note:
OPERATOR NOTE: DO NOT LAUNCH A DRAIN WHILE A CHAMBER JOB IS STILL RUNNING. My own practice error tonight, recorded because the symptom is confusing and the queue looks broken when it is not.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE:

    $ sluice-queue.sh list | awk '$5=="running"'
      running stage campaign/the-murrain  140dc49b94fc
      running merge campaign/the-sett     feccfd42e6d8

Two rows READING `running` under a queue whose whole design is one strictly serial claim. That is alarming for about thirty seconds.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE:

    pgrep -af sluice-run.sh
      1168196  req-140dc49b94fc-...     <- holds the staff, executing
      1170701  req-feccfd42e6d8-...     <- blocked on the flock, executing nothing

    census-run.sh status
      running sluice-stage:campaign/the-murrain @ 140dc49b...   pid 1168196

Both were CLAIMED and LAUNCHED; only one holds the staff. sluice-run.sh's own "queued for the staff (up to 7200s)" path is doing exactly its job, and the serialisation is intact. Nothing is corrupted and no candidate is at risk.

THE COST IS REAL BUT SMALL, and it is worth knowing rather than fixing: a blocked chamber process sits for up to two hours holding a row that reads `running` while doing nothing, so `sluice-status` overstates what the box is doing, and anyone attributing a slow queue would start from a false picture. Stack several drains and you get several.

THE DISCIPLINE, which costs one command:

    pgrep -f "[s]luice-run.sh" >/dev/null && echo "busy — do not drain" || bash scripts/sluice-drain.sh N

I have been draining with N>1 all evening, which is fine when the box is idle -- the loop claims and launches in sequence -- and sloppy when it is not. The flock has been absorbing my sloppiness rather than the queue being wrong about it.

Not proposing a code change. `running` meaning "claimed and launched" rather than "executing" is a defensible definition, and the alternative (a fourth state) buys less than it costs. The fix is the operator checking before draining, which is what this note is for.
